messages:
jin: FYI: observed micro-batch starvation on canary with multi-variant routing. suspect handshake prefilter for variant handoff is rejecting compatible queues early.

sam: saw same on prod-mock. p95 spikes when traffic has ~30% fallback to smaller variant. quick numbers: p50 48ms -> 70ms, p95 62ms -> 240ms. batch size median dropped 16->5.

leila: profile snippet attached. kernel selection toggles aggressively; kv-cache hit drops in the same windows. trace excerpt:
```
[trace 0x9aF3] kernel_switch: from=matmul_v1 to=matmul_v2 seq_len=128
[kv] lookup key=abc123 hit=false
[batch] formed_size=5 token_budget=72
latency_ms=238
```

maria: current queue policy uses `max_token_budget_per_queue: 80` and `handshake_timeout_ms: 2`. propose:
```
queue_policy:
  max_token_budget_per_queue: 140
  handshake_timeout_ms: 6
  handshake_prefilter_threshold: 0.2
```
This should let handshakes wait a bit to form larger slices.

sam: ran a local sim with those values -> p95 improved to 88ms, batch size median back to 14, kv-hit recovered to 68%. tradeoff: slight tail increase in single-variant steady flows.

jin: canary deploy? rolling 10% to dedicated pool to validate.

deploy-bot: deploy request: infra/eng-runtime job 'handshake-prefilter-canary' started by jin. canary id c-9082. Rolling to 10%.

leila: also add metrics: `handshake_prefilter_rejections` and `kernel_switch_count`. Alert if handshake_rejections > 500/min -> rollback.

sam: :thumbsup: I'll open a quick PR with sim harness + logs.

maria: thanks — I'll watch canary dashboards. if fallback ratio > 0.25 and p95>150 -> auto rollback.
